ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure is an ideal operational amplifier circuit. The inverting input terminal (−) is connected to a node; on the left side, this node is connected through a 1 kΩ resistor to a 2 V power supply, and above, it is connected through a 5 kΩ resistor in feedback to the output terminal Vout. The non-inverting input terminal (+) is connected to another node; on the left side, this node is connected through a 1 kΩ resistor to a 3 V power supply, and it is connected through an 8 kΩ resistor to ground. Reasoning: First find the voltage from the voltage divider circuit at the non-inverting terminal: V+ = 3 V × 8 kΩ / (1 kΩ + 8 kΩ) = 8/3 V. For an ideal operational amplifier under linear negative feedback, V− = V+ = 8/3 V. The inverting input terminal has no input current, so write KCL at the inverting node: (V− − 2)/1 kΩ + (V− − Vout)/5 kΩ = 0. Substitute V− = 8/3 to obtain (8/3 − 2)/1 kΩ + (8/3 − Vout)/5 kΩ = 0. Simplify: 2/3 + (8/3 − Vout)/5 = 0, so 10/3 + 8/3 − Vout = 0, giving Vout = 6 V.
